newsitem.title: USA: Weak US Treasuries edge up at noon, eye 5-yr sale.
newsitem.headline: Weak US Treasuries edge up at noon, eye 5-yr sale.

text.p: U.S. government securities cut some of their losses at noon, but garnered little direction from durable goods and housing data as dealers submitted bids for the Treasury's auction of 5-year notes.
Given the cheaper price going into the sale, the market should have little trouble digesting the comparatively small $11.5 billion in new paper, dealers said.

"Most of the money managers in street are extending their duration slightly but not going too crazy, so the five-year makes sense," said Greg Carr, bond market strategist at A.G. Edwards and Sons Inc.
"Also, it's a little smaller auction than usual that would, going into it, lead us to believe it might be a fairly decent auction," Carr said.
The deadline for bidding is 1300 EDT and results from the sale are expected around 1345 EDT.
At midday, the T-bond was down 6/32 at 98-30/32 with a yield of 6.71 percent. The five year was off 2/32 at 100-25/32, yielding 6.31 percent.
The bond hit a session low of 98-21/32, after getting a brief reprieve from overnight selling on the release of May durable goods orders, which fell 0.6 percent.
The fall contrasted with an expected rise of the same magnitude, and followed a upwardly revised 1.8 percent April jump.

But a surprising 4.4 percent increase in May existing home sales sent the T-bond nearly back to its lows. Home sales were at a 4.24 million annual rate, above 4.06 million in April and an expected 4.07 million in May.

U.S. debt instruments were knocked lower, along with the dollar/yen exchange rate overnight, after fears of higher Japanese interest rates were heightened by a robust tankan report on Japanese manufacturing activity, dealers said.
In early New York trade, selling by European investors looking to return to local markets weighed on Treasuries, dealers said.
In addition, a huge global issue of taxable bonds by the state of New Jersey prompted worries about market over-supply and talk of hedge sales of Treasuries.
But jitters may have abated amid reports the $2.8 billion multi-tranche issue was over subscribed, analysts said.
"It's holding in amazingly well," said Roseanne Briggen, bond analyst at MCM MoneyWatch.
"You're talking $2-3/4 billion hitting the market and in the old days we'd be down half a point but we're not. So, I don't think there is a lot of hedging going on in the issue," Briggen said.
Elsewhere the 10-year note was off 6/32 shortly after noon, priced at 101-12/32 with a yield of 6.43 percent.
In bills, the three-month was off two basis points at 4.99 percent and sixes were down four basis points at 5.04 percent.
